slides.title: A presentation the agent can keep editing
slides.subtitle: Treat the deck as a version-controlled visual document—not a finished binary file.

slides.title: The editable unit is the system
slides.statement: A deck becomes more useful when its source, evidence, design, and rendering can evolve together.
body: The agent can change a claim, re-render the slide, and inspect the result without leaving the project.

slides.title: Keep PowerPoint at the edge, not at the core
The workflow makes each transformation explicit
slides.takeaway: A deck is a pipeline from source material to a checked visual artifact.
slides.note: Ordinal stage values show sequence, not a performance benchmark.

slides.title: Research should leave a trace at every handoff

steps.title: Research
steps.copy: Collect files, repos, papers, data, and user context.

steps.title: Ground
steps.copy: Turn observations into claims with source IDs.

steps.title: Compose
steps.copy: Shape one primary message per slide.

steps.title: Verify
steps.copy: Run layout, screenshot, grounding, and PDF checks.

slides.title: Start with a small engine, then earn complexity

items.title: Content + evidence
items.copy: Make the authoring boundary legible to the next agent.

items.title: Stage + navigation
items.copy: Keep the design coordinate system fixed and predictable.

items.title: Components + SVG
items.copy: Reuse primitives without forcing every slide into one layout.

items.title: Checks + export
items.copy: Make the artifact testable before calling it finished.

slides.title: Every visual change should be reversible
slides.alt: A loop from source to slide to QA and back to source
slides.caption: A local SVG asset keeps the idea inspectable and offline-safe.
body: The screenshot is not the source. It is evidence that the source rendered as intended.

slides.title: Quality compounds when the system is explicit
slides.explanation: This is a design heuristic: remove any one factor and the deck becomes harder to trust or maintain.

slides.title: Version-controlled. Grounded. Programmable.
slides.subtitle: The next deck should be another project that the agent can understand, change, and verify.
